newsitem.title: USA: NY physical coffee - futures rally slows business.
newsitem.headline: NY physical coffee - futures rally slows business.

text.p: Activity on the New York physical coffee market remained sluggish, with roasters stepping aside after futures prices jumped some 18 percent in the week, traders said.
"I have not heard of a trade in 10 days," one dealer said. "The roaster community is just looking at the futures market and trying to figure out how they are going to price-fix."
CSCE March's ballooning premium to second-month May also soured roasters' appetite for the market, traders added, as producers were eager to price coffee against the spot contract.
The surge in coffee prompted leading U.S. roasters Maxwell House and Folgers to increase retail prices by 15 cents on their 13-ounce cans, effective next month.
But physical traders said another increase may not be far off. "It was too small," one trader said. "I think we will see a second round of price increases."
Despite the soaring futures and March's hefty premium to May, spot differentials held firm on the week.
The perception of coffee being held up due to a state workers strike in Colombia has kept differentials on Excelsos sky-high.
